claim: PTBP1 is a RNA-binding protein (RBP) expressed throughout B cell development.
source: Polypyrimidine tract-binding protein 1 (PTBP1) is a RNA-binding protein (RBP) expressed throughout B cell development.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by flow cytometry data showing PTBP1 expression across B cell developmental stages.

claim: Deletion of Ptbp1 in mouse pro-B cells results in upregulation of PTBP2 and normal B cell development.
source: Deletion of Ptbp1 in mouse pro-B cells results in upregulation of PTBP2 and normal B cell development.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data showing normal B cell numbers in P1sKO mice and PTBP2 expression in these cells.

claim: PTBP2 compensates for PTBP1 in B cell ontogeny.
source: We show that PTBP2 compensates for PTBP1 in B cell ontogeny as deletion of both Ptbp1 and Ptbp2 results in a complete block at the pro-B cell stage and a lack of mature B cells.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the complete block in B cell development in P1P2dKO mice compared to normal development in P1sKO mice.

claim: Deletion of both Ptbp1 and Ptbp2 results in a complete block at the pro-B cell stage and a lack of mature B cells.
source: We show that PTBP2 compensates for PTBP1 in B cell ontogeny as deletion of both Ptbp1 and Ptbp2 results in a complete block at the pro-B cell stage and a lack of mature B cells.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data showing absence of mature B cells and accumulation at pro-B cell stage in P1P2dKO mice.

claim: In pro-B cells PTBP1 ensures precise synchronisation of the activity of cyclin dependent kinases at distinct stages of the cell cycle.
source: In pro-B cells PTBP1 ensures precise synchronisation of the activity of cyclin dependent kinases at distinct stages of the cell cycle, suppresses S-phase entry and promotes progression into mitosis.
evidence: This is supported by data showing altered CDK activity markers (p-RB, p-SAMHD1) across cell cycle phases in P1P2dKO pro-B cells.

claim: PTBP1 suppresses S-phase entry in pro-B cells.
source: In pro-B cells PTBP1 ensures precise synchronisation of the activity of cyclin dependent kinases at distinct stages of the cell cycle, suppresses S-phase entry and promotes progression into mitosis.
evidence: This is demonstrated by increased proportions of P1P2dKO pro-B cells in S-phase compared to controls.

claim: PTBP1 promotes progression into mitosis in pro-B cells.
source: In pro-B cells PTBP1 ensures precise synchronisation of the activity of cyclin dependent kinases at distinct stages of the cell cycle, suppresses S-phase entry and promotes progression into mitosis.
evidence: This is supported by data showing accumulation of P1P2dKO pro-B cells in G2 phase with reduced pH3-positive cells indicating failure to enter mitosis.

claim: PTBP1 controls mRNA abundance and alternative splicing of CYCLIN-D2.
source: PTBP1 controls mRNA abundance and alternative splicing of important cell cycle regulators including CYCLIN-D2, c-MYC, p107 and CDC25B.
evidence: This is supported by mRNAseq data showing increased Ccnd2 mRNA abundance in P1P2dKO pro-B cells and PTBP1 binding to Ccnd2 3'UTR.

claim: PTBP1 controls mRNA abundance and alternative splicing of c-MYC.
source: PTBP1 controls mRNA abundance and alternative splicing of important cell cycle regulators including CYCLIN-D2, c-MYC, p107 and CDC25B.
evidence: This is supported by mRNAseq data showing increased Myc mRNA abundance and protein levels in P1P2dKO pro-B cells, with PTBP1 binding to Myc 3'UTR.

claim: PTBP1 controls mRNA abundance and alternative splicing of p107.
source: PTBP1 controls mRNA abundance and alternative splicing of important cell cycle regulators including CYCLIN-D2, c-MYC, p107 and CDC25B.
evidence: This is supported by mRNAseq data showing reduced Rbl1 mRNA abundance and altered splicing in P1P2dKO pro-B cells with PTBP1 binding near the alternatively spliced exon.

claim: PTBP1 controls mRNA abundance and alternative splicing of CDC25B.
source: PTBP1 controls mRNA abundance and alternative splicing of important cell cycle regulators including CYCLIN-D2, c-MYC, p107 and CDC25B.
evidence: This is supported by mRNAseq data showing reduced Cdc25b mRNA abundance in P1P2dKO pro-B cells and PTBP1 binding to Cdc25b 3'UTR.

claim: PTBP1 is an essential component of a previously unrecognised posttranscriptional mechanism controlling proliferation in pro-B cells.
source: Our results reveal a previously unrecognised mechanism mediated by a RBP that is essential for B cell ontogeny and integrates transcriptional and post-translational determinants of progression through the cell cycle.
evidence: This is supported by the comprehensive data showing PTBP1's role in controlling cell cycle progression through regulation of multiple mRNA targets.

claim: Igh-recombination at the pro-B cell stage typically occurs before Igl recombination in B cell ontogeny.
source: Igh-recombination at the pro-B cell stage typically occurs before Igl recombination in B cell ontogeny (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is established knowledge in B cell development supported by citation to Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Pro-B cells can be separated into fractions B and C according to Hardy's criteria.
source: Pro-B cells can be separated into fractions (Fr) B and C according to Hardy's criteria (Hardy et al., 1991), with D to J gene segment recombination occurring in FrB pro-B cells prior to V to DJ recombination in FrC pro-B cells (Hardy and Hayakawa, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hardy et al., 1991 and Hardy and Hayakawa, 2003.

claim: D to J gene segment recombination occurs in FrB pro-B cells prior to V to DJ recombination in FrC pro-B cells.
source: Pro-B cells can be separated into fractions (Fr) B and C according to Hardy's criteria (Hardy et al., 1991), with D to J gene segment recombination occurring in FrB pro-B cells prior to V to DJ recombination in FrC pro-B cells (Hardy and Hayakawa, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hardy and Hayakawa, 2003.

claim: Successful VDJ recombination of the Igh chain locus is coupled with a rapid proliferative expansion of early-pre-B cells (FrC').
source: Successful VDJ recombination of the Igh chain locus is coupled with a rapid proliferative expansion of early-pre-B cells (FrC') and the subsequent return to quiescence permissive for recombination at the Igl chain loci in late-pre-B cells (FrD) (Herzog et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Herzog et al., 2009.

claim: V(D)J recombination occurs during the G0/G1 phase of the cell cycle.
source: V(D)J recombination occurs during the G0/G1 phase of the cell cycle (Schlissel et al., 1993) and the RAG proteins, which are essential for V(D)J recombination, are degraded upon entry into S-phase, suppressing further recombination (Li et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Schlissel et al., 1993.

claim: RAG proteins are degraded upon entry into S-phase, suppressing further recombination.
source: V(D)J recombination occurs during the G0/G1 phase of the cell cycle (Schlissel et al., 1993) and the RAG proteins, which are essential for V(D)J recombination, are degraded upon entry into S-phase, suppressing further recombination (Li et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Li et al., 1996.

claim: The alternation between proliferative and non-proliferative stages during B cell development is precisely controlled to maintain genomic integrity.
source: The alternation between proliferative and non-proliferative stages during B cell development is precisely controlled to maintain genomic integrity (Herzog et al., 2009; Clark et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Herzog et al., 2009 and Clark et al., 2014.

claim: BTG2 and PRMT1 suppress proliferation in late-pre-B cells and allow Igl recombination.
source: Several factors have been identified that suppress proliferation in late-pre-B cells and allow Igl recombination. These include B cell translocation gene 2 (BTG2) and protein arginine methyl transferase 1 (PRMT1) (Dolezal et al., 2017), the signal transducers RAS (Mandal et al., 2009) and dual specificity tyrosine-regulated kinase 1A (DYRK1A) (Thompson et al., 2015) and the transcription factors interferon regulatory factor-4 and −8 (IRF4, IRF8) (Lu et al., 2003), IKAROS and AIOLOS (Ma et al., 2010), BCL-6 (Nahar et al., 2011) and FOXO3a (Herzog et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Dolezal et al., 2017.

claim: IL-7 promotes cell cycle progression in pro-B cells.
source: In pro-B cells, IL-7 promotes cell cycle progression (Clark et al., 2014) and the RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) ZFP36L1 and ZFP36L2 suppress proliferation, allowing Igh chain recombination and B cell development (Galloway et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Clark et al., 2014.

claim: ZFP36L1 and ZFP36L2 suppress proliferation in pro-B cells, allowing Igh chain recombination and B cell development.
source: In pro-B cells, IL-7 promotes cell cycle progression (Clark et al., 2014) and the RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) ZFP36L1 and ZFP36L2 suppress proliferation, allowing Igh chain recombination and B cell development (Galloway et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Galloway et al., 2016.

claim: By comparison to pre-B cells the mechanisms and genes that control proliferation in pro-B cells remain poorly understood.
source: Thus, by comparison to pre-B cells the mechanisms and genes that control proliferation in pro-B cells remain poorly understood.
evidence: This is an inference based on the review of known factors controlling proliferation in pre-B cells versus pro-B cells.

claim: FOXO1 is essential for progression after the pro-B cell stage and to induce expression of Rag genes.
source: Amongst these, FOXO1 is essential for progression after the pro-B cell stage and to induce expression of Rag genes (Dengler et al., 2008; Amin and Schlissel, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Dengler et al., 2008 and Amin and Schlissel, 2008.

claim: PTBP1 binds to Ptbp2 mRNA and, by inducing Ptbp2 exon 10 skipping, promotes NMD to suppress expression of PTBP2.
source: PTBP1 binds to Ptbp2 mRNA and, by inducing Ptbp2 exon 10 skipping, promotes NMD to suppress expression of PTBP2 (Boutz et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Boutz et al., 2007.

claim: PTBP1 and PTBP2 have specific and redundant roles.
source: PTBP1 and PTBP2 have specific and redundant roles and expression of PTBP2 in PTBP1-deficient cells compensates for many functions of PTBP1 (Spellman et al., 2007; Vuong et al., 2016; Ling et al., 2016; Monzón-Casanova et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Spellman et al., 2007; Vuong et al., 2016; Ling et al., 2016; Monzón-Casanova et al., 2018.

claim: Expression of PTBP2 in PTBP1-deficient cells compensates for many functions of PTBP1.
source: PTBP1 and PTBP2 have specific and redundant roles and expression of PTBP2 in PTBP1-deficient cells compensates for many functions of PTBP1 (Spellman et al., 2007; Vuong et al., 2016; Ling et al., 2016; Monzón-Casanova et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Spellman et al., 2007; Vuong et al., 2016; Ling et al., 2016; Monzón-Casanova et al., 2018.

claim: Deletion of Ptbp1 in pro-B cells results in normal B cell development accompanied by upregulated PTBP2 expression but important defects in germinal centre (GC) responses.
source: To study the unique roles of PTBP1 in B cells, we and others have deleted Ptbp1 in pro-B cells and found normal B cell development accompanied by upregulated PTBP2 expression but important defects in germinal centre (GC) responses (Monzón-Casanova et al., 2018; Sasanuma et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Monzón-Casanova et al., 2018 and Sasanuma et al., 2019.

claim: In GC B cells PTBP1 promotes the selection of B cell clones with high affinity antibodies, in part by promoting the c-MYC gene expression program induced upon positive selection following T cell help.
source: In GC B cells PTBP1 promotes the selection of B cell clones with high affinity antibodies, in part by promoting the c-MYC gene expression program induced upon positive selection following T cell help, and this function is not compensated by the upregulated PTBP2 (Monzón-Casanova et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Monzón-Casanova et al., 2018.

claim: PTBP3 is dispensable for B cell development.
source: We show that PTBP3 is dispensable for B cell development while PTBP1 and, in its absence PTBP2, are essential to promote B cell lymphopoiesis beyond the pro-B cell stage.
evidence: This is supported by data showing normal numbers of mature B cells in P3sKO mice.

claim: PTBP1 levels were similar across the different developing B cell populations.
source: PTBP1 levels were similar across the different developing B cell populations as the differences in fluorescence intensity for the anti-PTBP1 antibody, where early-pre B cells had the highest fluorescence intensity levels compared to the other stages in B cell development, were also found with the isotype control staining (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1B comparing PTBP1 staining to isotype control.

claim: PTBP2 protein was not detected in any of the B cell developmental stages analysed.
source: PTBP2 protein was not detected in any of the B cell developmental stages analysed (Figure 1).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1.

claim: PTBP3 was readily detected and expressed at similar amounts throughout the stages of B cell ontogeny.
source: PTBP3 was readily detected and also expressed at similar amounts throughout the stages of B cell ontogeny (Figure 1).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1.

claim: PTBP1 and PTBP3, but not PTBP2, are expressed throughout B cell development.
source: Thus, PTBP1 and PTBP3, but not PTBP2, are expressed throughout B cell development.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the flow cytometry data showing PTBP1 and PTBP3 expression but not PTBP2 expression.

claim: The numbers of mature B cells in the spleen of P3sKO mice were normal.
source: We found that the numbers of mature B cells in the spleen of P3sKO mice were normal (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: PTBP3-deficient B cells expressed PTBP1 and lacked PTBP2.
source: PTBP3-deficient B cells expressed PTBP1 and lacked PTBP2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: PTBP3 was dispensable for the development of B cells.
source: Therefore, PTBP3 was dispensable for the development of B cells and we focused on investigating the roles of PTBP1 during B cell development.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the normal B cell development observed in P3sKO mice.

claim: Conditional deletion of Ptbp1 in pro-B cells resulted in normal numbers of mature B cells.
source: Conditional deletion of a Ptbp1-floxed allele in pro-B cells mediated by a Cd79acre allele (Cd79acre/+;Ptbp1fl/fl mice, denoted here as Ptbp1 single conditional knock-out, P1sKO) resulted in normal numbers of mature B cells (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Deletion of Ptbp1 resulted in expression of PTBP2.
source: Deletion of Ptbp1 resulted in expression of PTBP2 (Figure 2B and Monzón-Casanova et al., 2018), as PTBP1 no longer promotes the degradation of Ptbp2 transcripts by NMD (Boutz et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2B and citation to Monzón-Casanova et al., 2018 and Boutz et al., 2007.

claim: Deletion of Ptbp2 alone had no impact on the number of mature B cells.
source: Deletion of Ptbp2 alone with the Cd79acre allele (P2sKO) had no impact on the number of mature B cells (Figure 2A), as expected since PTBP2 is not expressed during B cell development.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2A and the previous observation that PTBP2 is not expressed during B cell development.

claim: P1P2dKO mice lacked mature B cells in the spleen and lymph nodes.
source: P1P2dKO mice lacked mature B cells in the spleen and lymph nodes (Figure 2A, C and D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 2A, C, and D.

claim: PTBP1 plays an essential role in the development or maintenance of mature B cells that upon PTBP1 knockout is compensated by upregulation of PTBP2.
source: Thus, PTBP1 plays an essential role in the development or maintenance of mature B cells that upon PTBP1 knockout is compensated by upregulation of PTBP2.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the comparison of B cell development in P1sKO (normal) versus P1P2dKO (blocked) mice.

claim: P1P2dKO mice lacked immature and mature B cells as well as small late pre-B cells (Hardy's FrD).
source: Enumeration of cells at different stages of B cell development in the mouse bone marrow revealed that P1P2dKO mice lacked immature and mature B cells as well as small late pre-B cells (Hardy's FrD) (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figures 3A and B.

claim: P1P2dKO mice had slightly reduced numbers of FrB and FrC pro-B cells compared to littermate controls and to Cd79acre/+ 'Cre-only' mice.
source: P1P2dKO mice had slightly reduced numbers of FrB and FrC pro-B cells compared to littermate controls (Cd79a+/+;Ptbp1fl/fl;Ptbp2fl/fl, denoted here as 'control' unless stated otherwise) and to Cd79acre/+ 'Cre-only' mice (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 3A and B.

claim: In P1P2dKO mice FrC' early pre-B cells were not detected.
source: In P1P2dKO mice FrC' early pre-B cells, characterised by high expression of CD24 and CD249 (BP-1-positive) were not detected (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figures 3A and B.

claim: In the absence of PTBP1 and PTBP2, B cell development is blocked at the pro-B cell stage.
source: Thus, in the absence of PTBP1 and PTBP2, B cell development is blocked at the pro-B cell stage.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the flow cytometry data showing accumulation at pro-B cell stage and absence of later stages.

claim: P1P2dKO FrC pro-B cells had higher CD24 staining than control FrC pro-B cells.
source: P1P2dKO FrC pro-B cells had higher CD24 staining than control FrC pro-B cells (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: FrB and FrC P1P2dKO pro-B cells had high c-KIT levels and lacked CD2.
source: c-KIT (CD117) and CD2 staining showed that FrB and FrC P1P2dKO pro-B cells had high c-KIT levels and lacked CD2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), corroborating a block at an early developmental stage.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: In P1sKO compared to control and Cd79acre 'Cre-only' mice there was a ~3 fold increase in the numbers of early-pre-B cells.
source: In P1sKO compared to control and Cd79acre 'Cre-only' mice we noticed a ~ 3 fold increase in the numbers of early-pre-B cells (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The increase in early-pre-B cells in P1sKO mice is the result of higher CD43 staining in P1sKO developing B cells compared to control developing B cells.
source: This increase is the result of higher CD43 staining in P1sKO developing B cells compared to control developing B cells (Figure 3A), which leads to the inclusion of more cells in the CD43 high and CD25 low pro- and early pre-B cell gate (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is an interpretation based on flow cytometry data shown in Figures 3A and B.

claim: The numbers of pro-B cells were reduced by ~4.6 fold (FrB) and 19-fold (FrC) in P1P2dKO mice compared to Rag2-/- mice.
source: The numbers of pro-B cells were reduced by ~4.6 fold (FrB) and 19-fold (FrC) in P1P2dKO mice compared to Rag2-/- mice (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3B comparing P1P2dKO and Rag2-/- mice.

claim: Pro-B cells unable to recombine their Igh chain locus accumulated in the bone marrow whereas P1P2dKO pro-B cells did not.
source: Thus, pro-B cells unable to recombine their Igh chain locus accumulated in the bone marrow whereas P1P2dKO pro-B cells did not.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the comparison of pro-B cell numbers in Rag2-/- versus P1P2dKO mice.

claim: A few early-pre-B cells were present in P1P2dKO mice, indicating successful recombination of the Igh chain locus in P1P2dKO pro-B cells.
source: A few early-pre-B cells (B220+, CD19+, IgM-, CD93+, CD43high, Igμ+) were present in P1P2dKO mice, indicating successful recombination of the Igh chain locus in P1P2dKO pro-B cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data showing intracellular Igμ-positive cells in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The numbers of Igμ+ early-pre-B cells were decreased by ~13 fold in P1P2dKO mice in comparison to control mice.
source: However, the numbers of Igμ+ early-pre-B cells were decreased by ~13 fold in comparison to control mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: P1P2dKO pro-B cells did not express PTBP1 or PTBP2 protein, demonstrating efficient gene deletion.
source: P1P2dKO pro-B cells did not express PTBP1 or PTBP2 protein, demonstrating efficient gene deletion (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: P1P2dKO pro-B cells expressed increased amounts of PTBP3 compared to control pro-B cells.
source: P1P2dKO pro-B cells expressed increased amounts of PTBP3 compared to control pro-B cells (Figure 3C), yet in the absence of PTBP1 and PTBP2, PTBP3 expression was insufficient to promote B cell development.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: In the absence of PTBP1 and PTBP2, PTBP3 expression was insufficient to promote B cell development.
source: P1P2dKO pro-B cells expressed increased amounts of PTBP3 compared to control pro-B cells (Figure 3C), yet in the absence of PTBP1 and PTBP2, PTBP3 expression was insufficient to promote B cell development.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation that despite increased PTBP3, B cell development is still blocked in P1P2dKO mice.

claim: Deletion of Ptbp1 and Ptbp3 at the pro-B cell stage resulted in normal numbers of developing B cells in the bone marrow including normal numbers of immature B cells.
source: Deletion of Ptbp1 and Ptbp3 at the pro-B cell stage with the Ptbp1fl, Ptbp3 fl and Cd79acre alleles (P1P3dKO mice) resulted in normal numbers of developing B cells in the bone marrow including normal numbers of immature B cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Pro-B cells from P1P3dKO mice expressed PTBP2 and lacked both PTBP1 and PTBP3.
source: Pro-B cells from P1P3dKO mice expressed PTBP2 and lacked both PTBP1 and PTBP3 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: PTBP2 compensated for the absence of PTBP1 and PTBP3 during B cell development in the bone marrow.
source: Therefore, PTBP2 compensated for the absence of PTBP1 and PTBP3 during B cell development in the bone marrow.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the normal B cell development observed in P1P3dKO mice where PTBP2 is expressed.

claim: There is high redundancy between the different PTBP paralogs.
source: Our findings revealed high redundancy between the different PTBP paralogs which could reflect a requirement of certain amounts of total PTBP protein for the development of B cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation that different combinations of PTBP deletions can be compensated by remaining paralogs.

claim: There is an essential role for PTBP1 in B cell development at the pro-B cell stage that is compensated for by PTBP2, but not by PTBP3.
source: Importantly, we showed an essential role for PTBP1 in B cell development at the pro-B cell stage that is compensated for by PTBP2, but not by PTBP3.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the comparison of B cell development in different PTBP knockout combinations.

claim: More genes showed differential mRNA abundance when comparing P1P2dKO to control pro-B cells and P1P2dKO to P1sKO pro-B cells than when comparing P1sKO to control pro-B cells.
source: More genes showed differential mRNA abundance when comparing P1P2dKO to control pro-B cells and P1P2dKO to P1sKO pro-B cells than when comparing P1sKO to control pro-B cells (Figure 4A and Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by mRNAseq data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—source data 1.

claim: Almost one-quarter of the genes with increased or decreased mRNA abundance in P1P2dKO pro-B cells encoded transcripts that were directly bound by PTBP1 at the 3'UTR.
source: Almost one-quarter of the genes with increased or decreased mRNA abundance in P1P2dKO pro-B cells encoded transcripts that were directly bound by PTBP1 at the 3'UTR (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B and Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by integration of mRNAseq and iCLIP data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Ptbp2 mRNA abundance was increased ~18 fold in P1sKO compared to control pro-B cells.
source: A striking example of the latter effect is that Ptbp2 mRNA abundance was increased ~18 fold in P1sKO compared to control pro-B cells (Figure 4A) since Ptbp2 transcripts in P1sKO pro-B cells included exon 10 and were no longer degraded by NMD.
evidence: This is supported by mRNAseq data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The absence of both PTBP1 and PTBP2 in pro-B cells resulted in more changes in AS than the absence of PTBP1.
source: Similar to our observations on mRNA abundance, the absence of both PTBP1 and PTBP2 in pro-B cells resulted in more changes in AS than the absence of PTBP1 (Figure 4B and Figure 4—source data 2).
evidence: This is supported by alternative splicing analysis shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—source data 2.

claim: From 30% to 50% of the events with AS changes when comparing P1P2dKO to control pro-B cells were bound by PTBP1.
source: From 30% to 50% of the events with AS changes when comparing P1P2dKO to control pro-B cells were bound by PTBP1 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2D and Figure 4—source data 2) implicating PTBP1 in controlling these events directly.
evidence: This is supported by integration of alternative splicing and iCLIP data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2D.

claim: There is a small overlap of genes with changes in mRNA abundance and also AS in the different pairwise comparisons.
source: There is a small overlap of genes with changes in mRNA abundance and also AS in the different pairwise comparisons (Figure 4C), suggesting that the inclusion of certain exons generates NMD targets.
evidence: This is supported by Venn diagram analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: 1021 and 611 genes had decreased and increased mRNA abundance, respectively, in P1P2dKO compared to control and P1sKO pro-B cells.
source: We identified 1021 and 611 genes with decreased and increased mRNA abundance, respectively, in P1P2dKO compared to control and P1sKO pro-B cells (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by hierarchical clustering analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claim: 971 genes had increased or decreased inclusion levels of at least one event in P1P2dKO pro-B cells compared to control and P1sKO.
source: Amongst AS changes, we found 971 genes with increased or decreased inclusion levels of at least one event in P1P2dKO pro-B cells compared to control and P1sKO (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by hierarchical clustering analysis shown in Figure 4E.

claim: P1P2dKO pro-B cells clustered separately from P1sKO and control pro-B cells when considering abundance changes.
source: P1P2dKO pro-B cells clustered separately from P1sKO and control pro-B cells when considering abundance changes (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by hierarchical clustering shown in Figure 4D.

claim: When analysing AS, P1P2dKO and P1sKO pro-B cells clustered together but separately from control pro-B cells.
source: When analysing AS, P1P2dKO and P1sKO pro-B cells clustered together but separately from control pro-B cells (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by hierarchical clustering shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The compensatory functions of PTBP2 when PTBP1 is absent were more evident when considering mRNA abundance than AS.
source: Therefore, the compensatory functions of PTBP2 when PTBP1 is absent were more evident when considering mRNA abundance than AS.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the clustering patterns observed for mRNA abundance versus AS.

claim: In pro-B cells, PTBP2 has only a few specific targets and mostly compensates for the absence of PTBP1.
source: Therefore, in pro-B cells, PTBP2 has only a few specific targets and mostly compensates for the absence of PTBP1, while PTBP1 ensures the appropriate expression at the level of AS and mRNA abundance of more than 2000 genes.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the small number of genes uniquely regulated in P1sKO versus the large number regulated in P1P2dKO.

claim: PTBP1 ensures the appropriate expression at the level of AS and mRNA abundance of more than 2000 genes.
source: Therefore, in pro-B cells, PTBP2 has only a few specific targets and mostly compensates for the absence of PTBP1, while PTBP1 ensures the appropriate expression at the level of AS and mRNA abundance of more than 2000 genes.
evidence: This is based on the total number of genes with differential expression in P1P2dKO compared to controls.

claim: Ebf1 mRNA abundance was reduced ~1.5 fold in P1P2dKO compared to control and P1sKO pro-B cells.
source: Ebf1 mRNA abundance was reduced ~1.5 fold in P1P2dKO compared to control and P1sKO pro-B cells (Figure 5A), but this should not impact B cell development because Ebf1 haploinsufficiency results in normal B cell ontogeny (Vilagos et al., 2012; Györy et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by mRNAseq data shown in Figure 5A and citations to Vilagos et al., 2012 and Györy et al., 2012.

claim: Foxo1 mRNA abundance was reduced ~1.7 fold in P1P2dKO compared to P1sKO and control pro-B cells.
source: Foxo1 mRNA abundance was reduced ~1.7 fold in P1P2dKO compared to P1sKO and control pro-B cells (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by mRNAseq data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: PTBP1 bound directly to the 3'UTR of Foxo1, indicating a direct role of PTBP1 stabilising Foxo1 mRNA.
source: PTBP1 bound directly to the 3'UTR of Foxo1 (Figure 5B), indicating a direct role of PTBP1 stabilising Foxo1 mRNA.
evidence: This is supported by iCLIP data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Il7r mRNA abundance was reduced ~1.4 fold in P1P2dKO compared to P1sKO and control pro-B cells.
source: Indeed, Il7r mRNA abundance was reduced ~1.4 fold in P1P2dKO compared to P1sKO and control pro-B cells (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by mRNAseq data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: IL-7 receptor staining was similar between P1P2dKO and control pro-B cells.
source: However, IL-7 receptor staining was similar between P1P2dKO and control pro-B cells (Figure 5C), ruling out a role for a reduction of IL-7 receptor in the developmental defect of P1P2dKO pro-B cells.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The known essential elements of the B cell development programme are independent of the PTBP.
source: These data indicate that the known essential elements of the B cell development programme, including three targets of FOXO1, are independent of the PTBP.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation that key B cell development genes are not significantly affected in P1P2dKO pro-B cells.

claim: P1P2dKO FrB pro-B cells had a reduced mRNA abundance of Cdkn1b, Cdkn1c, Cdkn2c and Cdkn2d compared to control and P1sKO FrB pro-B cells.
source: We found that P1P2dKO FrB pro-B cells had a reduced mRNA abundance of Cdkn1b, Cdkn1c, Cdkn2c and Cdkn2d (encoding p27, p57, p18 and p19, respectively) compared to control and P1sKO FrB pro-B cells (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is supported by mRNAseq data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The reduction in mRNA abundance of CDK inhibitors is likely to be an indirect effect of the lack of PTBP1 and PTBP2 at least partly mediated through direct FOXO1 regulation.
source: Thus, the reduction in mRNA abundance of CDK inhibitors is likely to be an indirect effect of the lack of PTBP1 and PTBP2 at least partly mediated through direct FOXO1 regulation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known role of FOXO1 in promoting p27 expression and the reduced FOXO1 levels in P1P2dKO cells.

claim: There was an increase in the proportions of FrB and FrC pro-B cells that are in S-phase (2-fold in FrB and 4-fold in FrC) in P1P2dKO compared to control and P1sKO mice.
source: We found an increase in the proportions of FrB and FrC pro-B cells that are in S-phase (2-fold in FrB and 4-fold in FrC) in P1P2dKO compared to control and P1sKO mice (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is supported by EdU incorporation data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: G0/G1 P1P2dKO pro-B cells had increased FSC-A measurements compared to P1sKO and control G0/G1 pro-B cells.
source: Moreover, G0/G1 P1P2dKO pro-B cells had increased FSC-A measurements compared to P1sKO and control G0/G1 pro-B cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C), which are indicative of an increased cell size and are consistent with a high biosynthetic capacity and a predisposition to enter S-phase.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: In P1P2dKO pro-B cells the proportions of early-S-phase cells were increased 4.7-fold compared to control and 3.2-fold compared to P1sKO pro-B cells.
source: In P1P2dKO pro-B cells the proportions of early-S-phase cells were increased 4.7-fold compared to control and 3.2-fold compared to P1sKO pro-B cells (Figure 6B and C).
evidence: This is supported by EdU/BrdU double labeling data shown in Figures 6B and C.

claim: P1P2dKO pro-B cells enter S-phase more readily than control pro-B cells but they fail to progress through S-phase at the same pace as PTBP1-sufficient pro-B cells.
source: This indicated that P1P2dKO pro-B cells enter S-phase more readily than control pro-B cells but they fail to progress through S-phase at the same pace as PTBP1-sufficient pro-B cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the increased proportions of cells in early S-phase and the smaller increase in post S-phase cells.

claim: Compared to control and P1sKO, P1P2dKO pro-B cells in G2/M-phase were increased both in proportion (~40 fold) and number (~8 fold).
source: Compared to control and P1sKO, P1P2dKO pro-B cells in G2/M-phase were increased both in proportion (~40 fold) and number (~8 fold) (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: The proportion of pH3-positive cells amongst P1P2dKO FrB pro-B cells with 4N-DNA content was reduced ~3 fold compared to the proportions found amongst P1sKO and control FrB pro-B cells.
source: The proportion of pH3-positive cells amongst P1P2dKO FrB pro-B cells with 4N-DNA content was reduced ~3 fold compared to the proportions found amongst P1sKO and control FrB pro-B cells (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is supported by phospho-histone H3 staining data shown in Figure 6G.

claim: The majority of P1P2dKO pro-B cells with 4N-DNA content were in G2-phase and had not entered mitosis.
source: Therefore, the majority of P1P2dKO pro-B cells with 4N-DNA content were in G2-phase and had not entered mitosis.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the reduced pH3 staining in cells with 4N DNA content.

claim: PTBP1, and in its absence PTBP2, were required for pro-B cells to progress from G2 to M-phase of the cell cycle.
source: PTBP1, and in its absence PTBP2, were thus required for pro-B cells to progress from G2 to M-phase of the cell cycle.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the accumulation of P1P2dKO pro-B cells in G2 phase.

claim: p27 staining was reduced ~1.7 fold in G0/G1 P1P2dKO FrB pro-B cells compared to G0/G1 P1sKO and control FrB pro-B cells.
source: We found p27 staining reduced ~1.7 fold in G0/G1 P1P2dKO FrB pro-B cells compared to G0/G1 P1sKO and control FrB pro-B cells (Figure 7A and B), consistent with the decreased Cdkn1b mRNA abundance in FrB pro-B cells (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figures 7A and B.

claim: In G2 cells p27 staining was increased ~7 fold in P1P2dKO FrB pro-B cells compared to P1sKO and control FrB pro-B cells.
source: In contrast, in G2 cells p27 staining was increased ~7 fold in P1P2dKO FrB pro-B cells compared to P1sKO and control FrB pro-B cells (Figure 7A and B).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figures 7A and B.

claim: Proportions of both p-RB and p-SAMHD1-positive cells were increased in FrB and FrC P1P2dKO G0/G1 pro-B cells compared to control and P1sKO G0/G1 pro-B cells.
source: Proportions of both p-RB and p-SAMHD1-positive cells were increased in FrB and FrC P1P2dKO G0/G1 pro-B cells compared to control and P1sKO G0/G1 pro-B cells (Figure 7C and D, and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B) indicating an abnormally high CDK activity in G0/G1 P1P2dKO pro-B cells.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figures 7C, D, and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Amongst pro-B cells in G2/M-phases the proportions of p-RB and p-SAMDH1-positive cells were reduced in P1P2dKO mice compared to control and P1sKO mice.
source: In contrast, amongst pro-B cells in G2/M-phases the proportions of p-RB and p-SAMDH1-positive cells were reduced in P1P2dKO mice compared to control and P1sKO mice (Figure 7C and D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figures 7C, D, and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: PTBP1 is essential for controlling the activity of CDKs in different phases of the cell cycle in pro-B cells, to limit entry into S-phase and to promote entry into mitosis.
source: Thus, PTBP1 is essential for controlling the activity of CDKs in different phases of the cell cycle in pro-B cells, to limit entry into S-phase and to promote entry into mitosis.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the CDK activity measurements across different cell cycle phases.

claim: S- and G2/M-associated transcripts were not globally increased in P1P2dKO FrB pro-B cells compared to control and P1sKO FrB pro-B cells.
source: S- and G2/M-associated transcripts were not globally increased in P1P2dKO FrB pro-B cells compared to control and P1sKO FrB pro-B cells (Figure 8A and Figure 8—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of cell cycle-associated gene expression shown in Figure 8A.

claim: The majority of the changes observed in the transcriptome of P1P2dKO compared to control and P1sKO pro-B cells are not the result of comparing populations with different proliferative status, but are reflective of an altered pro-B cell transcriptome.
source: This indicates that the majority of the changes observed in the transcriptome of P1P2dKO compared to control and P1sKO pro-B cells are not the result of comparing populations with different proliferative status, but are reflective of an altered pro-B cell transcriptome.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the lack of global increase in cell cycle-associated transcripts.

claim: Myc and Ccnd2 showed increased mRNA abundance in P1P2dKO compared to P1sKO and control FrB pro-B cells.
source: Two genes (Myc and Ccnd2) whose proteins promote entry into S-phase, showed increased mRNA abundance in P1P2dKO compared to P1sKO and control FrB pro-B cells (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is supported by mRNAseq data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: Btg2 and Rbl1 had reduced mRNA abundance in P1P2dKO compared to control and P1sKO FrB pro-B cells.
source: Two further genes (Btg2 and Rbl1), whose proteins inhibit S-phase entry, had reduced mRNA abundance in P1P2dKO compared to control and P1sKO FrB pro-B cells (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is supported by mRNAseq data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: There was an increase of c-MYC protein abundance in G0/G1 P1P2dKO FrB pro-B cells compared to control and P1sKO G0/G1 FrB pro-B cells.
source: PTBP1 bound to the 3'UTR of Myc (Figure 8—figure supplement 1), and we confirmed an increase of c-MYC protein abundance in G0/G1 P1P2dKO FrB pro-B cells compared to control and P1sKO G0/G1 FrB pro-B cells (Figure 8C and D) as the fold-change increase in fluorescence intensity of the c-MYC staining (2.2-fold) was greater than the fold-change increase in fluorescence intensity of the control staining (1.5-fold).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figures 8C and D.

claim: In pro-B cells PTBP1 suppresses c-MYC.
source: Therefore, in pro-B cells PTBP1 suppresses c-MYC.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the increased c-MYC levels in P1P2dKO pro-B cells and PTBP1 binding to Myc 3'UTR.

claim: Ccnd2 abundance was increased ~2 fold in P1P2dKO compared to control and P1sKO FrB pro-B cells.
source: Ccnd2 abundance (encoding CYCLIN-D2) was increased ~2 fold in P1P2dKO compared to control and P1sKO FrB pro-B cells (Figure 8B) and PTBP1 bound to the Ccnd2 3'UTR (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by mRNAseq data shown in Figure 8B and iCLIP data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: PTBP1 and PTBP2 could reduce Ccnd2 mRNA abundance indirectly by suppressing c-MYC-mediated transcription and directly by binding its mRNA.
source: c-MYC induces transcription of Ccnd2 (Bouchard et al., 2001). Therefore, PTBP1 and PTBP2 could reduce Ccnd2 mRNA abundance indirectly by suppressing c-MYC-mediated transcription and directly by binding its mRNA.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known role of c-MYC in inducing Ccnd2 transcription and PTBP1 binding to Ccnd2 mRNA.

claim: Btg2 mRNA abundance was reduced ~2 fold due to Ptbp1 and Ptbp2 deletion in FrB pro-B cells.
source: Btg2 mRNA abundance was reduced ~2 fold due to Ptbp1 and Ptbp2 deletion in FrB pro-B cells (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is supported by mRNAseq data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: PTBP1 could directly promote BTG2 expression in FrB pro-B cells by stabilising Btg2 transcripts.
source: No obvious change in Btg2 AS was detected but PTBP1 binding sites were present at the Btg2 3'UTR (Figure 8—figure supplement 1). Therefore, PTBP1 could directly promote BTG2 expression in FrB pro-B cells by stabilising Btg2 transcripts.
evidence: This is an inference based on PTBP1 binding to Btg2 3'UTR shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: Rbl1 mRNA abundance was reduced ~1.5 fold in P1P2dKO compared to control and P1sKO pro-B cells.
source: Rbl1 mRNA abundance was reduced ~1.5 fold in P1P2dKO compared to control and P1sKO pro-B cells (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is supported by mRNAseq data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: PTBP1 and PTBP2 suppress the inclusion of a downstream alternative 5' splice site (A5SS) in Rbl1 exon 8.
source: PTBP1 and PTBP2 suppress the inclusion of a downstream alternative 5' splice site (A5SS) in Rbl1 exon 8. Use of this A5SS in P1P2dKO FrB pro-B cells generates an NMD-target isoform (Figure 8E).
evidence: This is supported by mRNAseq visualization shown in Figure 8E.

claim: This A5SS event in Rbl1 is conserved in human.
source: This A5SS event is conserved in human, as PTBP1- and PTBP2-depleted HeLa cells (Ling et al., 2016) also have an increased usage of the downstream A5SS compared to PTBP-sufficient cells, resulting in reduced RBL1 mRNA abundance (Figure 8F and G).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of published HeLa cell data shown in Figures 8F and G.

claim: PTBP1 most likely promotes Rbl1 expression by suppressing production of the NMD-targeted Rbl1 isoform.
source: Therefore, PTBP1 most likely promotes Rbl1 expression by suppressing production of the NMD-targeted Rbl1 isoform.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the alternative splicing data and conservation in human cells.

claim: Deregulated expression of Myc, Ccnd2, Btg2 and Rbl1 in the absence of PTBP1 and PTBP2 would act to drive entry of pro-B cells into S-phase.
source: Collectively, deregulated expression of Myc, Ccnd2, Btg2 and Rbl1 in the absence of PTBP1 and PTBP2 would act to drive entry of pro-B cells into S-phase.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the known roles of these genes in cell cycle regulation and their altered expression in P1P2dKO cells.

claim: The abundance of Cdc25b, Ect2, Kif2c and Kif22 was reduced (~3,~5,~2 and~2 fold, respectively) in P1P2dKO compared to control and P1sKO FrB pro-B cells.
source: The abundance of Cdc25b, Ect2, Kif2c and Kif22 was reduced (~3,~5,~2 and~2 fold, respectively) in P1P2dKO compared to control and P1sKO FrB pro-B cells (Figure 9A).
evidence: This is supported by mRNAseq data shown in Figure 9A.

claim: PTBP1 probably promotes Cdc25b expression by binding to its 3'UTR and enhancing its stability in pro-B cells.
source: Cdc25b AS was unaffected by PTBP1 and PTBP2 absence but PTBP1 bound to the Cdc25b 3'UTR (Figure 4—source data 2 and Figure 8—figure supplement 1). Thus, PTBP1 probably promotes Cdc25b expression by binding to its 3'UTR and enhancing its stability in pro-B cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on PTBP1 binding to Cdc25b 3'UTR and lack of AS changes.

claim: In P1P2dKO pro-B cells an Ect2 alternative exon with two alternative 3'SS was found more frequently included compared to P1sKO and control pro-B cells.
source: In P1P2dKO pro-B cells an Ect2 alternative exon with two alternative 3'SS was found more frequently included compared to P1sKO and control pro-B cells (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is supported by mRNAseq visualization shown in Figure 9B.

claim: Inclusion of the Ect2 AS exon will generate transcripts predicted to be degraded by NMD.
source: Inclusion of this AS exon, using either of the two alternative 3'SS, will generate transcripts predicted to be degraded by NMD.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the splicing pattern and prediction of NMD.

claim: KIF2c and KIF22 have increased inclusion of an exon that generates predicted NMD-targets in P1P2dKO compared to P1sKO and control pro-B cells.
source: Both have increased inclusion of an exon that generates predicted NMD-targets in P1P2dKO compared to P1sKO and control pro-B cells and some evidence for PTBP1 binding in adjacent regions (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is supported by mRNAseq visualization shown in Figure 9B.

claim: PTBP1 promoted expression of genes important for mitosis by suppressing AS linked to NMD (Ect2, Kif2c, Kif22) and by stabilizing mRNA (Cdc25b).
source: These data indicated that PTBP1 promoted expression of genes important for mitosis by suppressing AS linked to NMD (Ect2, Kif2c, Kif22) and by stabilizing mRNA (Cdc25b).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the molecular mechanisms observed for these genes.

claim: The altered expression of Ect2, Kif2c, Kif22, and Cdc25b in the absence of PTBP1 and PTBP2 is likely to contribute to the high proportions of G2 cells observed in P1P2dKO pro-B cells.
source: The altered expression of these genes in the absence of PTBP1 and PTBP2 is likely to contribute to the high proportions of G2 cells observed in P1P2dKO pro-B cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known roles of these genes in mitosis and their altered expression.

claim: PTBP1 is a regulator of the cell cycle in pro-B cells.
source: Taken together, our findings implicate PTBP1 as a regulator of the cell cycle in pro-B cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on all the cell cycle-related findings.

claim: PTBP1 is essential to control appropriate expression of an mRNA regulon dictating CDK activity, progression to S-phase and entry into mitosis.
source: PTBP1 is essential to control appropriate expression of an mRNA regulon dictating CDK activity, progression to S-phase and entry into mitosis (Figure 9C).
evidence: This is a conclusion summarized in the model shown in Figure 9C.

claim: In the absence of PTBP1 and its partially redundant paralog PTBP2, the molecular control of the cell cycle in primary pro-B cells is disrupted and B cell development is halted.
source: In the absence of PTBP1 and its partially redundant paralog PTBP2, the molecular control of the cell cycle in primary pro-B cells is disrupted and B cell development is halted.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on all the findings showing disrupted cell cycle control and blocked B cell development.

claim: The enhanced entry into S-phase of pro-B cells was only observed when both PTBP1 and PTBP2 were absent.
source: The enhanced entry into S-phase of pro-B cells was only observed when both PTBP1 and PTBP2 were absent.
evidence: This is based on the comparison of cell cycle phenotypes in P1sKO versus P1P2dKO mice.

claim: The role of PTBP1 in suppressing S-phase entry was unanticipated since in other systems, including GC B cells, PTBP1 promoted proliferation.
source: The role of PTBP1 in suppressing S-phase entry was unanticipated since in other systems, including GC B cells, PTBP1 promoted proliferation (Suckale et al., 2011; Shibayama et al., 2009; La Porta et al., 2016) and progression through late S-phase (Monzón-Casanova et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies showing PTBP1 promoting proliferation.

claim: The role of PTBP1 in promoting G2 transition into mitosis is conserved in other systems.
source: Similar to our findings in pro-B cells, PTBP1-deficient GC B cells and embryonic stem cells also had increased proportions of cells in G2/M phases of the cell cycle (Monzón-Casanova et al., 2018; Shibayama et al., 2009). Therefore, the role of PTBP1 in promoting G2 transition into mitosis is conserved in other systems.
evidence: This is supported by citations to studies in other cell types showing similar G2/M accumulation.

claim: The components of the cell cycle mRNA regulon are expressed in both mature and pro-B cells.
source: Shared and specific mechanisms will control the cell cycle in mature and pro-B cells but the components of this cell cycle mRNA regulon are expressed in both mature and pro-B cells (Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by expression data shown in Table 1.

claim: Direct binding of PTBP1 to the targets of the cell cycle mRNA regulon is expected in pro-B cells.
source: Therefore, direct binding of PTBP1 to these targets is expected in pro-B cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the expression of these genes in both cell types and iCLIP data from mature B cells.

claim: The proteins encoded within the cell cycle mRNA regulon interact with each other to generate feed-forward activation loops that promote cell cycle entry and mitosis.
source: The proteins encoded within this mRNA regulon interact with each other to generate feed-forward activation loops that promote cell cycle entry and mitosis.
evidence: This is based on known interactions between these cell cycle regulators.

claim: c-MYC suppresses Cdkn1b (encoding p27).
source: For example, c-MYC suppresses Cdkn1b (encoding p27) (Yang et al., 2001) and increases Ccnd2 transcription (Bouchard et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yang et al., 2001.

claim: c-MYC increases Ccnd2 transcription.
source: For example, c-MYC suppresses Cdkn1b (encoding p27) (Yang et al., 2001) and increases Ccnd2 transcription (Bouchard et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Bouchard et al., 2001.

claim: CYCLIN-D2 promotes nuclear export and degradation of p27/CDKN1b.
source: CYCLIN-D2 promotes nuclear export and degradation of p27/CDKN1b (Susaki et al., 2007) and p27 directly inhibits CYCLIN-D-CDK4/6 complexes (Yoon et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Susaki et al., 2007.

claim: p27 directly inhibits CYCLIN-D-CDK4/6 complexes.
source: CYCLIN-D2 promotes nuclear export and degradation of p27/CDKN1b (Susaki et al., 2007) and p27 directly inhibits CYCLIN-D-CDK4/6 complexes (Yoon et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yoon et al., 2012.

claim: The block at G2 in P1P2dKO pro-B cells resulted mainly from increased p27 expression.
source: Although the block in G2-phase we observed could have resulted from a response to DNA damage we found little evidence for enhanced DNA damage in FrB pro-B cells (data not shown). This data suggested that the block at G2 in P1P2dKO pro-B cells resulted mainly from increased p27 expression.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the lack of DNA damage evidence and the observed increase in p27 in G2 cells.

claim: The net outcome from deregulation of the PTBP1 controlled cell cycle mRNA regulon in the absence of PTBP1 and PTBP2 is an enhanced CDK activity in G0/G1 pro-B cells that drives entry into S-phase and a reduced CDK activity amongst blocked G2 pro-B cells.
source: The net outcome from deregulation of the PTBP1 controlled cell cycle mRNA regulon in the absence of PTBP1 and PTBP2 is an enhanced CDK activity in G0/G1 pro-B cells that drives entry into S-phase and a reduced CDK activity amongst blocked G2 pro-B cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion summarizing the cell cycle phenotypes observed.

claim: Absence of PTBP1 and PTBP2 in FrC pro-B cells resulted in the same defects in proliferation as in FrB pro-B cells.
source: Absence of PTBP1 and PTBP2 in FrC pro-B cells resulted in the same defects in proliferation as in FrB pro-B cells.
evidence: This is stated based on observations in both FrB and FrC pro-B cells.

claim: Alterations in the progression through the cell cycle in both FrB and FrC fractions contributed to the block in B cell development in the whole pro-B cell population.
source: Thus, alterations in the progression through the cell cycle in both fractions contributed to the block in B cell development in the whole pro-B cell population.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the similar phenotypes in both pro-B cell fractions.

claim: FrC pro-B cells lacking PTBP1 and PTBP2 had an increase in c-MYC expression at the G0/G1 stage and increased p27 expression at G2.
source: FrC pro-B cells lacking PTBP1 and PTBP2 also had an increase in c-MYC expression at the G0/G1 stage and increased p27 expression at G2.
evidence: This is stated based on observations in FrC pro-B cells.

claim: The molecular mechanisms by which PTBP1 controls the cell cycle and promotes B cell development in pro-B cells were conserved in both pro-B cell fractions.
source: Therefore, the molecular mechanisms by which PTBP1 controls the cell cycle and promotes B cell development in pro-B cells were conserved in both pro-B cell fractions.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the similar molecular phenotypes in FrB and FrC pro-B cells.

claim: The role found for PTBP1 and PTBP2 is distinct from that of other RBPs such as AUF1 and ELAVL1 which, when deleted, have little effect on B cell development.
source: The role that we have found here for PTBP1 and PTBP2 is distinct from that of other RBPs such as AUF1 (Sadri et al., 2010) and ELAVL1 (Diaz-Muñoz et al., 2015) which, when deleted, have little effect on B cell development.
evidence: This is supported by citations to studies on AUF1 and ELAVL1.

claim: The absence of ZFP36L1 and ZFP36L2 has a much milder impact on B cell development than does the combined absence of PTBP1 and PTBP2.
source: The ZFP36 family members ZFP36L1 and ZFP36L2 are important for quiescence during lymphocyte development, but their absence has a much milder impact on B cell development (Galloway et al., 2016) than does the combined absence of PTBP1 and PTBP2.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Galloway et al., 2016 and comparison to the severe phenotype in P1P2dKO mice.

claim: The unique role found for PTBP1 in controlling the cell cycle, and its redundancy with PTBP2, further underscores the importance of post-transcriptional RNA regulation as an essential component of the molecular regulation of the cell cycle.
source: The unique role that we have found for PTBP1 in controlling the cell cycle, and its redundancy with PTBP2, further underscores the importance of post-transcriptional RNA regulation as an essential component of the molecular regulation of the cell cycle.
evidence: This is a conclusion emphasizing the significance of the findings.

claim: In the context of B cells, post-transcriptional regulation by PTBP1 is essential for developmental progression beyond the pro-B cell stage.
source: In the context of B cells this regulation is essential for developmental progression beyond the pro-B cell stage.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the block in B cell development at the pro-B cell stage in P1P2dKO mice.
